Subject: Launch next week — short notice quota bump?

Hi Sean,

Quick note — our pilot goes live for the patient triage flow on Friday (2027-05-14) and we expect a burst during initial rollout to 3k users. Engineering is concerned the current sandbox quotas won't cover peak traffic (we're seeing load tests that spike to ~180 req/s with typical message lengths). Can Redwood support a short-term quota increase and a temporary routing exception to avoid 429s during the first 48 hours?

Attached is a quick spike forecast (CSV) and our rollout cadence. We're happy to accept a short feature-flagged canary or slowdown knobs if that helps. Need to coordinate on monitoring and a rollback plan.

Thanks — appreciate any fast-turn help.

Emily Tran

Product asks/questions for infra:
- Can we provision a temporary dedicated pool or route to a higher-throughput variant for 48 hours?
- Any constraints on KV cache warming given the patient triage templates are stable (should help hit 60% cache reuse).
- What telemetry/alerts do we need to give them to detect regressions quickly?

Neha — can you confirm the uplift approval timeline and any quota ticket template you prefer?
Karthik/David — feasible to reserve a surge lane or toggle routing policy for a single account for a weekend window?

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Launch next week — short notice quota bump? — Velox Health (quick sync)

Thanks for the heads up. A few clarifying items from runtime:
- Is Velox using streaming responses or single shot? Streaming increases connection concurrency and planning differs.
- Can they segment traffic by route/intent? If we can route only the triage endpoint to a higher tier, that reduces blast radius.
- Sequence length of 700 is large — we'll want to ensure GPUs have the right memory profile. If they can trim prompt templates (or we offer dynamic truncation at tail), that will reduce peak token cost.

Technically we can provision a temporary surge lane (short-lived Dedicated shard) but it requires a capacity commit or an explicit surge credit approval. Operationally we can also add a routing override that shifts traffic to the high-throughput variant for the account for 48 hours (no infra deploy). That is quicker but will increase per-token cost.

If Emily confirms streaming=false and they can provide a per-minute RPS distribution bucketed by 5-min windows, we can finalize whether routing override is enough or we need the temporary shard.

I can take the routing override path as a fallback. Neha — are we comfortable with an ad-hoc surge credit for this case?

—Karthik
Principal Infra PM, Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Launch next week — short notice quota bump? — Velox Health (approval path)

Quick process note: we can approve a temporary quota uplift if the customer provides:
- 5-min bucketed RPS for a 2-hour peak window + 24-hour lookback baseline
- Average and 95th percentile token lengths (prompt + completion)
- A signed SLA-exception request (I attached the usual PDF form below)

Approval timeline: if we get the above within 4 hours we can push an uplift ticket that goes through ops review and be actioned within 12-18 hours. For a same-day turnaround (they asked EOD), routing override (Karthik's suggestion) is the fastest — we can apply and monitor.

Note on monitoring: we'll add a temporary dashboard for their account and set alert thresholds on 429 rate (>0.1%), p50/p95 latency shifts, and token-cost burn rate. If the boost pushes utilization near hard capacity, we'll throttle and initiate automatic fallback to the next-compatible model.

I'll draft the uplift ticket once we have the CSV in the format above. Marissa — please coordinate contract/billing terms if this becomes a paid surge.

—Neha
Capacity & Reliability, Redwood Inference
